Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:10:1.english: This is not severance - For all her days she is bound to him to fulfill this condition on his account.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:10:2.hebrew: הרי זה כריתות - אפילו מיד, דהיא תקיים תנאו ותלך, שאפשר דברים הללו לבא לידי הבדלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:10:2.english: This is an act of severance - Even immediately, for she will fulfill his condition and go [her way], as it is possible for these matters to come to a separation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:11:1.hebrew: מכרת כריתות - דהוה מצי למיכתב ספר כרת, דמשמע ספר כורתה, והך דרשא אחריתי — מייתורא דלישנא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:11:1.english: From [the distinction between] karet [and] keritut - For [the verse] could have written sefer karet, which would mean “a scroll severs her”; and this other exposition [is derived] from the superfluous phrasing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:12:1.hebrew: חדא מחדא לא אתיא כו' - הכי קשיא ליה: האי תנא דלעיל, דפריך בכולהו "והלא דין הוא", והדר דלא אתו מדינא ואצרכיה קרא — למה לי קרא בכולהו? נהי דחדא מחדא לא אתיא, תיתי חדא מתרתי במה מצינו, בהצד השוה שבהן: שקונין בעלמא וקונין כאן, אף אני אביא את השלישי! שהרי כולם קונים במקום אחר: כסף ושטר קונה באמה העבריה, כדלקמן (קידושין דף יד:); ביאה קונה ביבמה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:12:1.english: One cannot be derived from one, etc. - This is what was difficult to [the Gemara]: As for this Tanna above, who challenged regarding all of them, "Is this not logical deduction?", and then [concluded] that they cannot be derived by logical deduction and required a verse [for each] — why do I need a verse for all of them? Granted that one [mode] cannot be derived from one [other], let one be derived from two by [the principle of] mah matzinu [inference from precedent], through their common denominator: that they effect acquisition elsewhere and they effect acquisition here, so too I will bring [derive] the third [mode]! For all of them effect acquisition in another context: money and a document acquire a Hebrew maidservant, as [stated] below (Kiddushin 14b); [and] intercourse acquires a yevama.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:12:2.hebrew: כסף וביאה הנאתן מרובה - אבל שטר אירוסין אין בו לה שום הנאה, שהרי אין כתוב בו אלא ״הרי את מקודשת לי״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:12:2.english: Money and intercourse, their benefit is great - But a document of betrothal has no benefit in it for her, for nothing is written in it other than: “Behold, you are betrothed to me.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:13:1.english: Their acquisition is great - For they acquire land and slaves.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:14:1.hebrew: בע"כ - ביאה קונה ביבמה בע"כ, דנפקא לן ביבמות (דף נד.) מויבמה; וכן שטר מוציא את האשה בע"כ מבעלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:14:1.english: Against her will - Intercourse acquires a yevama against her will, as we derive in Yevamot (54a) from “and perform the levirate marriage with her” [Deuteronomy 25:5]; and similarly, a document [of divorce] releases a woman from her husband against her will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:15:1.english: In [the case of] a Hebrew maidservant against her will - For her father sells her without her consent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:16:1.hebrew: כסף שאינו מאכיל בתרומה - אם נתארסה לכהן, כדתנן בכתובות (דף נז:): אין האשה אוכלת בתרומה עד שתכנס לחופה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:16:1.english: Money, which does not enable [the wife] to partake of teruma - If she was betrothed to a priest, as we learned in a mishna in Ketubot (57b): “A woman may not partake of teruma until she enters the wedding canopy.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:19:1.english: Which does not complete - To remove her from her father's authority with regard to her earnings and her inheritance.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:2:1.hebrew: שטר שאין פודין בו הקדשות - אם כתב לגזבר שטר על מעות פדיון הקדש, אין הקדישו פדוי, דבעינן ״ונתן הכסף וקם לו״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:2:1.english: A document, with which one cannot redeem consecrated property - If one wrote a document to the [Temple] treasurer for the redemption money of consecrated property, his consecrated property is not redeemed, for we require: “And he will give the money and it will be assured to him.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:5:1.hebrew: האי שטרא לחוד והאי שטרא לחוד - בזה כתוב לשון כניסה, וזה מפורש לשון יציאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:5:1.english: This document is discrete and this document is discrete - In this one is written the language of entry [into marriage], and in this one is specified the language of departure [from marriage].

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:5:2.hebrew: האי כספא לחוד - כשהוא נותנו, מפרש על מנת מה הוא נותנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:5:2.english: This money is discrete - When he gives it, he specifies for what purpose he is giving it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:5:3.english: Is one - It is not mentioned within it whether to release [i.e., divorce] or to bring in [i.e., betroth].

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:7:1.english: Referring to divorce and excluding [a mode of] betrothal - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:8:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who derives a different exposition from this [phrase] “and he writes” - In the second chapter of Gittin (21b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:9:1.hebrew: לדבר הכורת - שיהא הספר מבדילן, ולא שיהא בו תנאי האוגדן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 5a:9:1.english: For a matter that severs - That the document [of divorce] should separate them, and not that there should be a condition in it that binds them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:10:1.hebrew: על מנת שלא תלכי לבית אביך לעולם אין זה גט - פירש בקונטרס: שכל ימיה נאגדת לקיים תנאי זה מחמתו. וא"ת: אמאי לא אמר דהוי גט? שהרי אם מת אביה, יכולה היא ליכנס לבית ושוב אינה נאגדת בו, דלאחר מיתת אביה לא חשיב בית אביה, כדאמרינן בנדרים (דף מו.): "קונם לביתך שאיני נכנס", מת או מכרו — מותר. וי"ל: דבית אביה קרוים כל יוצאי חלציו של אביה, אע"ג שמת, כדכתיב (בראשית ל״ח:י״א) גבי תמר: "שבי אלמנה בית אביך", אע"פ שמת אביה, כדמוכחי קראי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:10:1.english: "On the condition that you will never go to your father’s house, that is not a [valid] bill of divorce" - The Kunteres [Rashi] explained that all her days she remains bound to fulfill this condition on his account. And if you say: Why does [the baraita] not say that it is a [valid] bill of divorce? For if her father dies, she can enter the house and is no longer bound to him, since after her father's death it is not considered her father's house, as we say in Nedarim (46a): "[Entering] your house is konam for me, that I will not enter," [if the owner] died or sold it, [he is] permitted [to enter]. And one can say that all the offspring of her father are called "her father's house," even though he died, as it is written regarding Tamar (Genesis 38:11): "Remain a widow in your father’s house," even though her father had died, as the verses prove.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:11:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי הגלילי מכרת כריתות נפקא - תימה: דבפרק המגרש (גיטין ד' פג:) קאמר על רבנן דר"א בן עזריה: "כרת כריתות לא דרשי", ור' יוסי הגלילי בכלל דרבנן; והכא אמר דר' יוסי הגלילי דרש כרת כריתות! וי"ל, דלא קאמר "לא משמע להו", אלא "דלא דרשי" — פירוש: לההוא דרשא דהתם, דמיבעי להו לדרשא דהכא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:11:1.english: "And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili derives it from karet [and] keritut" - This is puzzling: for in chapter HaMegaresh (Gittin 83b), [the Gemara] says concerning the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah: "They do not expound [the distinction between] karet [and] keritut," and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili is included among [those] Rabbis! Yet here, [the Gemara] says that Rabbi Yosei HaGelili expounds [the distinction between] karet [and] keritut! And one can say: [the Gemara] did not say "it does not imply [anything] to them," but rather "they do not expound [it]" — meaning: [they do not expound it] for that exposition over there, because they need it for the exposition here.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:14:1.hebrew: שכן ישנן בעל כרחה - פי' בקונטרס: ביאה — ביבמה, שטר — בגרושין, כסף — באמה העבריה. וקשה לרבינו תם: אם זה חשוב בעל כרחה, מה שהאב מוכר את בתו בעל כרחה — א"כ, מאי קאמר רב הונא לקמיה: "כסף באישות מיהא לא אשכחן בע"כ"? הלא האב מקדש בתו קטנה בכסף בע"כ! ואומר רבינו תם: כיון דאב במקום בתו קאי, אין זה חשוב בע"כ, כיון שהוא מדעתו של אב. וא"ת: א"כ, היכי קאמר: "כסף נמי איתא באמה העבריה בע"כ"? הרי אב מוכרה מדעתו! וי"ל: דהכי פריך, כסף איתא באמה בע"כ — כגון שהאדון מייעד את העבריה בכסף מקנתה, בע"כ של אב ובע"כ של בת; דהא דאמר לקמן (קידושין דף יט.): "אשר לא יעדה" — שצריך לייעדה, לא שצריך לעשות מרצונה, אלא שצריך להודיעה שלשם קידושין מייעדה. ואע"ג דאמר לקמן: "באישות מיהא לא אשכחנא", ובכי האי גוונא שמייעד הוי אישות — מ"מ, בתחילה לא בא הכסף בשביל אישות. ויש מיישבים פי' הקונטרס: דודאי זה קרוי בעל כרחה — מכירה של אמה העבריה, שחוב הוא לה, ואם היתה בת דעת לא היתה מתרצית; אבל קידושי קטנה לאו חוב הוא לה כמו מכירה, וסופה עומדת לינשא, אם היתה בת דעת היתה מתרצית, ולא חשיב על כרחה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:14:1.english: "For they apply against her will" - The Kunteres [Rashi] explains: Intercourse [applies against her will] in [the case of] a yevama, a document in divorce, [and] money in [the case of] a Hebrew maidservant. And Rabbeinu Tam finds this difficult: If this is considered "against her will" — that the father sells his daughter against her will — if so, why does Rav Huna say later [5b]: "In any event, with regard to marriage, we do not find [money effective] against her will"? Behold, a father betroths his minor daughter with money against her will! And Rabbeinu Tam says: Since the father stands in place of his daughter, this is not considered "against her will," since it is with the father's consent. And if you say: If so, how can [the Gemara] say: "Money is also [found effective] in [the case of] a Hebrew maidservant against her will"? Behold, the father sells her with his consent! And one can say that this is what [the Gemara] challenges: Money is found [effective] in [the case of a Hebrew] maidservant against her will — such as where the master designates the Hebrew maidservant [for marriage] with the money of her purchase, against the father's will and against the daughter's will. For that which [the Gemara] says below (Kiddushin 19a): "'who did not designate her' — which teaches that he must designate her" — [this means] not that he must do so with her consent, but rather that he must inform her that he is designating her for the purpose of betrothal. And even though [the Gemara] says below: "In marriage at any rate we do not find [it]," and in such a case where he designates her it is marriage — nevertheless, initially the money did not come for the purpose of marriage. And some resolve the Kunteres's explanation: Certainly that is called "against her will" — the sale of a Hebrew maidservant — for it is a disadvantage to her, and if she were of mature understanding she would not have consented; but the betrothal of a minor girl is not a disadvantage to her like sale, and ultimately she is destined to marry, [so] if she were of mature understanding she would have consented, and [therefore] it is not considered "against her will".

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:1:1.hebrew: ומניין שאף בשטר - ומק"ו דאמה העבריה, שאין נקנית בביאה ונקנית בשטר — ליכא למימר. חדא — משום דאמה גופה, מדאיתקש לאחרת נפקא לן לקמן (קידושין דף טז.). ואפילו לרב חסדא, דיליף לה מ"לא תצא כצאת העבדים" — אבל נקנית היא בקנין העבדים — איכא למיפרך כדלעיל: שכן יוצאה בכסף. ועוד — דכיון דלרב חסדא אב כותבו, ליכא למילף באשה, שאינה נקנית בזה הענין, שהבעל כותבו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:1:1.english: "And from where [is it derived] that [a woman is acquired] even by a document?" - And [to suggest deriving this] from an a fortiori inference [kal vaḥomer] from a Hebrew maidservant—who cannot be acquired through sexual intercourse, yet is acquired through a document—cannot be said. First, because [the rule that] the maidservant herself [is acquired through a document] is derived for us later (Kiddushin 16a) from [the fact] that she is juxtaposed to "another" [woman, i.e., a free wife]. And even according to Rav Ḥisda, who derives it from: "She shall not go out as the male slaves do" (Exodus 21:7)—[meaning] but she can be acquired through the mode of acquisition of [Canaanite] slaves—it can be refuted as above: for she [the Hebrew maidservant] can be released with money. And furthermore, since according to Rav Ḥisda the father writes it [the document of sale], one cannot derive [from this regarding] a woman, who is not acquired in this manner, as the husband writes it.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:2:1.hebrew: שכן פודין בו הקדשות ומעשר - וא"ת: כל זה אשים בק"ו — ומה כסף, שאע"פ שפודין בו הקדש ומעשר ואינו מוציא, ואפ"ה מכניס; שטר, שאע"פ שאין פודין בו הקדש מוציא, אינו דין שיכניס?! י"ל: דחומרא הכתובה בפסוק אין להכניס בק"ו, דודאי חומרא של סברא ניתנה להשים בק"ו; אבל הכתובה — יש לנו לומר שהיא הגורמת מעלה. וא"ת: ונימא ק"ו מקרקעות, שאינן מוציאות, אפ"ה מכניסות — פי': דאדם יכול לקדש אשה בקרקע ואינה מתגרשת בקרקע, והתם ליכא למיפרך שכן פודין בו הקדש! וי"ל: דאיכא למיפרך: מה לקרקע שכן קונין מטלטלין אגבן, תאמר בשטר?! וא"ת: מטלטלין יוכיחו, שאין קונין אגבן, ואינן מוציאות, ומכניסות — אף אני אביא שטר! וי"ל: מה למטלטלין שכן פודין בו הקדש:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:2:1.english: "As one can redeem with it consecrated property and tithe" - And if you say: I can incorporate all of this into the kal va-chomer: Just as [with regard to] money, even though one redeems with it consecrated property and [second] tithe, it does not release [a woman from marriage], and even so it brings [her] in [effects betrothal]; a document, which, even though one does not redeem with it consecrated property, releases [her from marriage], is it not logical that it should bring [her] in? It can be answered: A stringency written in a verse cannot be incorporated into a kal va-chomer. For certainly a stringency [derived by] logical reasoning can be placed into a kal va-chomer, but regarding one that is written [in Scripture], we must say that it is what causes the advantage [of money, enabling it to effect betrothal]. And if you say: Then let us derive a kal va-chomer from land, which does not release, yet nevertheless brings in — explanation: for a person can betroth a woman with land, but she is not divorced with land — and there, one cannot refute [the derivation by saying] "as one can redeem with it consecrated property"! It can be answered: One can refute [this as well]: What [is unique] about land is that one can acquire movable property along with it [via kinyan agav]; will you say [the same regarding] a document?! And if you say: Movable property will prove [otherwise], for one does not acquire [other property] along with them, and they do not release, yet they bring in; so too I will bring [the case of] a document! It can be answered: What [is unique] about movable property is that one can redeem consecrated property with it.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:3:1.hebrew: מה הויה בכסף אף יציאתה בכסף - ולענין ביאה ליכא למימר: "מה הויה בביאה, אף יציאתה בביאה" — שלהתרחק ממנה הוא מגרשה; ועוד, משום שמצא בה ערות דבר רגיל לגרשה, ואז יש לו לפרוש:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:3:1.english: "Just as becoming is through money, so too her leaving is through money" - And regarding sexual intercourse, it cannot be said: "Just as becoming is through sexual intercourse, so too her leaving is through sexual intercourse" — for it is in order to distance himself from her that he divorces her; and furthermore, because it is on account of having found in her an unseemly matter [ervat davar] that one typically divorces her, and in that case he must separate [from her].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:4:1.hebrew: סניגור יעשה קטיגור - וא"ת: א"כ, היכי קאמר לעיל: "מה לאמה העבריה שכן יוצאה בכסף, ודין הוא שתהא נקנית בכסף"? אדרבה, גריעותא — דאין קטיגור נעשה סניגור! וי"ל: דבאמה העבריה ליכא למימר הכי, לפי שמתחלה, שאביה מוכרה לשפחות, הוא מקבל הכסף מן האדון; א"כ, כשהוא רוצה לפדותה, דין הוא שיקבל האדון הכסף. אבל איש שמקדש אשה, הכל בא על ידו, בין הקידושין בין הגירושין — והתם שייך למיפרך: "יאמרו כסף מכניס" וכו':
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:4:1.english: "Can an advocate become a prosecutor?" - And if you say: If so, how can [the Gemara] say earlier: "What about a Hebrew maidservant, as she is released with money, and [so] it is logical that she should be acquired with money"? On the contrary, [this is] a disadvantage, for a prosecutor does not become an advocate! And one can answer: In the case of a Hebrew maidservant, one cannot say this, because initially, when her father sells her into maidservanthood, he receives the money from the master; if so, when [the father] wishes to redeem her, it is logical that the master should receive the money. However, [regarding] a man who betroths a woman, everything comes through him, both the betrothal and the divorce — and there it is pertinent to object: "People will say: Money brings in..." etc.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:7:1.hebrew: קאי בגירושין ממעט גירושין - ואין סברא לומר: "קאי בכתיבה וממעט בכתיבה" — דפשטא דקרא משמע שבא לומר דוקא בכתיבה; דקאמר: "אם לא תמצא חן בעיניו וכתב לה" — משמע דוקא בזה הענין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 5a:7:1.english: "[The verse is] referring to divorce, [so it] excludes divorce" - And it is not reasonable to say: "[The verse is] referring to writing, [so it] excludes writing" [from betrothal] — for the plain meaning of the verse indicates that it comes to say [divorce is effected] specifically through writing, as it says: "If she does not find favor in his eyes... and he writes for her," which implies [that divorce may be effected] specifically in this manner.
